title: AI & Chip Investment Momentum (Nvidia, Palantir)
summary: Gotrade News - AI chip stocks remain at the center of investor attention, with Nvidia (NVDA) quoted at $228.87, up 0.66%, and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
body_markdown:
The Motley Fool's Geoffrey Seiler argues that Nvidia "will remain the leader" in training, where its CUDA software moat "still holds strong today."


In inference, however, he writes that the work is less technically demanding and Nvidia's CUDA moat "is not nearly as wide," opening room for rivals. Seiler discloses positions in AMD and Broadcom, so his view should be read as one analyst's opinion rather than a consensus call.

On AMD, the article points to lower-cost GPUs, an improved ROCm software platform, and existing multiyear deals with OpenAI and Meta, with Anthropic and Microsoft among more recent customers.


Broadcom, per the same report, leads in custom ASICs, co-designed Alphabet's TPUs, and is projected to generate $115 billion in AI revenue next fiscal year and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. These projections are forecasts, not guaranteed outcomes.


## Palantir Nears Top of $166 to $188 Range


On the software side, Palantir shares traded at $183.03, according to[24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/22/wall-streets-palantir-price-targets-tell-an-interesting-story/) , after a roughly 60% rally from June lows of $106.37 to a peak of $207.52. The move was driven by Q2 revenue growth of 92.83% year over year and a 149% jump in U.S. commercial revenue.


Valuation remains the key debate. As reported by 24/7 Wall St., Palantir trades at a forward P/E of 79x versus 27x for ServiceNow, and the outlet's $185.99 price target implies only about 1.6% upside, with a bull case of $213.74 and a bear case of $158.91.


Analysts have nonetheless revised FY2027 EPS estimates up 26 times in 30 days with zero cuts, and the outlet rates the stock a Hold.


## What the AI Chip Split Means for Investors


Taken together, the data points to AI demand broadening across the stack, from Nvidia's training dominance to inference hardware and enterprise AI software.


Readers tracking the sector can compare this with recent[AI chip and semiconductor momentum across SK Hynix, Nvidia, Arm, ASML, and Analog Devices](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/news/ai-chip-semiconductor-momentum-sk-hynix-nvidia-arm-asml-analog-devices/) . Elevated valuations, particularly for Palantir, mean the stocks can remain volatile even when fundamentals are strong.
